Colleagues, this past Saturday, Canada and the world witnessed the coronation of His
Majesty King Charles III and Her Majesty Queen Camilla.
The coronation of Their Majesties was a historic occasion for our country and the Canadian
people as well as the entire Commonwealth as King Charles III has become the first new
sovereign and head of state for Canada in seven decades.
On behalf of Kitchener City Council and the residents of the City of Kitchener, I extend
congratulations to His Majesty King Charles III and Her Majesty Queen
Camilla on the occasion of the coronation. King Charles III has dedicated
his entire life to public service including diversity, environment and
sustainability and we wish him continued health, strength and inspiration
throughout his reign. To commemorate the coronation of His Majesty King Charles
III and Her Majesty Queen Camilla, the City of Kitchener lit Carls Air Square
emerald green and offered free community skates and public swims
this past weekend. The lighting of Carl's Air Square saw Kitchener join other
cities across Canada and throughout the Commonwealth in a national illumination
initiative that was coordinated by the Canadian Department of Heritage. His
Majesty's King Charles III's coronation emblem is green and white and green is
associated with the environment which has been an important cause for His
Majesty. Following Saturday's coronation the Commonwealth is now headed by His
Majesty King Charles III, and Canada will join other member countries in continuing to work
together to advance shared values of democracy, peace and prosperity. As a country, we will
continue to collaborate to make life better for people and advocate for the representation
of small and vulnerable nations on the global stage, and Canada and the Commonwealth nations
will continue to make strides in promoting democratic governance, environmental protection,
and sustainable development.
